boundary_rationale: The same speech-introduction verb reopens with a comparative statement, then pivots into command: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.11, byte tier) — Yahweh said to me, “Backsliding Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah” (web:Jer.3.11), continuing directly into הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier) — “Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, ‘Return, you backsliding Israel,’ says Yahweh” (web:Jer.3.12) — a go-and-proclaim imperative carrying the shuv invitation. The address turns from singular to plural already inside this same verse, at לֽוֹא אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), and again one verse later at וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier). The plural vocative call that follows, שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier), resumes this same plural address rather than opening it afresh, and stays inside this unit on that resumption; the number at all three sites is a single-witness byte reading, the second witness rendering the address number-blind throughout. The promised restoration (shepherds, the ark forgotten, Jerusalem as Yahweh's throne, Judah and Israel reunited: web:Jer.3.15-18) and Yahweh's own reflection on disappointed hope (web:Jer.3.19-20) continue inside the same speech opened at Jer.3.11, with no fresh word-event or messenger-formula onset anywhere inside the span. A narrated scene shift — a voice heard weeping, rather than reported divine speech — opens the next unit at Jer.3.21.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at Jer.3.19 was considered, where the emphatic independent pronoun before a perfect verb, וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier), marks a pivot in the divine reflection; it was rejected for lacking a word-event formula, koh-amar onset, or imperative of the kind that bounds this book's other seams, so the reflection is kept inside the larger invitation-and-promise unit at reduced confidence rather than split on that pivot alone. A closer rival was also weighed at Jer.3.14, where the plural vocative call שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) resumes rather than opens the plural address begun at Jer.3.12; it was likewise not adopted, since no tier-1 onset of this book's own kind accompanies the resumption.

device_notes: A petuchah at Jer.3.10 falls immediately before this span opens (single-witness, tier-3); a setumah falls inside the span at Jer.3.17, between the restoration promise's individual clauses, disclosed here as interior texture rather than adopted as a cut given the absence of any formula or imperative there. Two ketiv/qere notes stand at MT 3:19, one of the book's twelve doubled-note verses (single-witness): the ketiv/qere pairs תקראו תִּקְרְאִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier) and תשובו תָשֽׁוּבִי (oshb:Jer.3.19, byte tier), each a second-person number alternation. The meshuvah noun recurs twice more here, at web:Jer.3.11 and web:Jer.3.12, continuing the wordplay named in the unit before this one.

boundary_rationale: A narrated scene, not reported divine speech, opens this unit: ק֚וֹל עַל שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.3.21, byte tier) — “A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the children of Israel; because they have perverted their way, they have forgotten Yahweh their God” (web:Jer.3.21) — shifting from the first-person divine promise of the preceding unit to third-person description of a sound. Yahweh’s call, שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים אֶרְפָּ֖ה מְשׁוּבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.22, byte tier) — “Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your backsliding” (web:Jer.3.22) — is answered inside the same unit by the community’s own first-person-plural confession, “Behold, we have come to you” (web:Jer.3.22) through “we have sinned against Yahweh our God” (web:Jer.3.25), closing “We have not obeyed Yahweh our God’s voice” (web:Jer.3.25). This same three-word call, שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙, stands at Jer.3.14 (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) — identical to the call quoted above at skeleton tier and distinct at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses); the shared call argues continuity across this unit's front seam, which is carried instead by the speaker turn at Jer.3.21. A conditional address to ‘Israel’ by name, resuming Yahweh’s own voice, opens the next unit at Jer.4.1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Jer.3.22's imperative opening as the true onset, with web:Jer.3.21 held back as the close of the preceding restoration promise, was considered and rejected: the voice-heard-weeping scene lacks an addressee or formula tying it to the prior unit's promise, and it motivates the call and confession that follow it rather than concluding what precedes it.
